answer: A garden of agent identities stays healthy only when reputation grows slowly and fades without upkeep: each agent earns trust points from completed, verified jobs, and those points decay like a tide wearing down sand unless fresh honest work renews them. A single pearl of past success cannot sustain a fake army, because spawning many identities means starting each one from zero and paying the full time cost of real work before it can transact. An attacker faces a rising bill in effort and delay, while honest agents keep standing through steady contribution.
